chapter: Second session: boyhood, brothers and early road years
title: Selling newspapers as a boy
summary: He sold the Record, Times, Herald and Express starting at Fifth and Central, explaining the prices and his two cents profit.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: When you first got to L.A., can you remember your first impressions of the city--what it looked like?
What did I know about impressions? I was about...let's see...'88...about seven years old.
Do you remember thinking it was different in some ways...You don't remember your first impressions of Los Angeles?
No, no, I don't remember anything about that.
But almost immediately you started selling newspapers. Is that right?
Yeah. Started selling newspapers. I wasn't here a week hardly before I started selling newspapers.
And the paper you sold was The Record. Is that right?

The Record, Times, and The Herald and The Express. And I first started out selling papers at the old Pacific Railroad 'cause it was right at Fifth and Central there, and we lived at Fourth Street, and I sold it at catching people coming off the train and going to the train, you see. Which I sold, make me fifty ...sixty cents every afternoon after school, you know. That's pretty good for a kid ten or eleven years old.
Sure. How much did the paper sell for then?

Well, we sold the...The Record was a cent, and The Express was two cents, and The Times was a nickel. So we used to...it got customary that people didn't want change...didn't bother about change. We sold The Express and The Record two-for-a-nickel. That was a general thing all over town but it was...the... if you bought 'em and had pennies, you could get 'em for three cents, you know, but people didn't want to be bothered with pennies, you know, so they'd give you a nickel, say "Give me two-for-a-nickel," so we sold them two-for-a-nickel. And The Times and The Herald was a nickel.
So how much did you get from selling a nickel paper? If you sold The Times or Herald, how much of it did you get?
I think it cost us three cents.
So you made two cents on a paper.
Made two cents on a paper, yeah.
